increment_paragraph: **RULE37-PILOT (pluggable-cards seam B, P2 pilot 2).** The [card](../../reports/rule37-pilot/README.md) moves gateway rule 37 into its own package, `crates/gateway-rules/rule-37-result-constructors`, behind the gateway rule interface, and registers its run-time switch. The typed `sizeof` exemption becomes the arm `sizeof-operand-exemption` at `aggregate_store::store_bases`: the host's existing typed operand reader computes the checked spans, and the package admits them only when they are well formed. The `asserted_allocation` premise becomes the arm `asserted-allocation-premise` at `legacy_checked_spec::settle`. A checked specification naming that premise stands only while rule 37 admits it, with `Obligation::Premise("asserted_allocation")`, which the declaration must state; this is the interface's first premise obligation. The null readers' checked-result guard stays in the host and is never switched off. Two additive, vocabulary-free host capabilities (`CheckedOperandArm`, `SpecificationPremiseArm`) are added to `qcore-gateway-rule-api`. `QCORE_GATEWAY_RULES_OFF=37` counts every `sizeof` mention again, which is the scan before rule 37, and withdraws `rd_calloc` and `rd_strdup`. Their callers then see only W4's summary of an in-unit body, a stated boundary (RULE37-W4-ASSERT-PREMISE-VISIBILITY). Lean `QCore.ResultConstructorSwitch` (13 audited theorems) states that on is the rule, off is the old reading and off never widens. Identity: `quirin-audit measure` against the published baseline `80c8aea98` matches the declared `none` on all three routes, with 0 moved and 0 content-changed rows. Every differing artifact is equal up to a checked bijective substitution of the revision and its derived digests (corpus 218 values, system 6, slice 4). Contribution by switch (first committed ledgers, `contract/contributions/37/`, consistent): eight-home has 5 librdkafka rows Unknown -> Safe, all under `asserted_allocation` (`rd_kafka_ConsumerGroupListing_new`, `_copy`, `_copy_opaque`, `rd_kafka_AlterUserScramCredentials_result_response_new`, `rd_kafka_acl_result_new`); system and slice have none. Card gate on `a5ef39093` (full mode): Rust 8,858 passed, 0 failed, 15 ignored (575 units); fmt, Clippy and probes exit 0; Lean 391 audits; Python 554 tests with 1 failure, the committed matrix's derived `lean_audits` (390 against 391 files), which the landing's matrix regeneration resolves. Parity cost for plan decision 6: about 1,140 added lines for about 10 lines of rule code, 0.8 h of implementation, a 2.6 h gate and 13.5 h of mostly slot-queued measurement.

ledger.title: W4 summaries of asserting wrappers carry no named build premise
ledger.text: With rule 37 off (QCORE_GATEWAY_RULES_OFF=37), the checked specifications of rd_calloc and rd_strdup are withdrawn, which is the existing W45 withdrawal. Their callers then see what W4 validates from the in-unit asserting body: a non-null result through the enabled assert's terminating call. A caller with no sizeof, such as rd_calloc(1, 16) in tests/rule37_switch.rs, therefore stays Safe on that summary, and its row names no asserted_allocation premise. This is no Unknown-to-Safe by the migration, since the row is Safe with 37 on too. It also predates rule 37 for any undeclared asserting wrapper. But it means the deployed-build fact rule 37 makes explicit for a declared specification is only implicit, as the analysed-build assumption, for a W4-inferred one. DISCHARGE: decide whether a W4 summary that rests on a terminating assertion must carry a named premise (and implement it with an identity or measured run), or record that it rests on the standing analysed-build assumption.

RULE37-PILOT (2026-10-29) migrated rule 37 to crates/gateway-rules/rule-37-result-constructors. It ran an identity run against baseline 80c8aea98 (declared none on all routes, with a checked bijective revision/digest substitution) and wrote switch-measured ledgers (eight-home +5 Safe, system 0, slice 0); registry id 37 is now known to known_rule. It added two vocabulary-free capabilities (CheckedOperandArm, SpecificationPremiseArm). The checked-specification settlement has no route-map position, so its premise arm is registered at classification, by its effect. Remaining: 35 (RULE35-PILOT, concurrent), 36, 33, 34 and 32a.
